verdict.rationale: Gmail documents standard IMAP, POP and SMTP access for non-Gmail clients, with OAuth 2.0 authorization, and says it syncs messages and labels into Outlook, Apple Mail and Thunderbird. The export half of the story is not evidenced: the API mentions 'read-only mail extraction, indexing, and backup' and account migration, but no standards-based export format (such as mbox). Community reports say Gmail's IMAP is imperfect (IDLE does not propagate read-status changes, and IMAP clients need hacks to map Gmail IDs), which limits depth but does not negate IMAP access. Missing for 10: JMAP support, a documented standards-based export format, and faithful full-fidelity IMAP sync of flag/read state.

support.subject: As a switcher, my mail stays reachable over open protocols and standard formats — IMAP/JMAP/SMTP access and standards-based export — so no client can lock me in

citations.quote: En el caso de los clientes que no son de Gmail, Gmail admite los protocolos estándar IMAP, POP y SMTP.
The Gmail IMAP, POP, and SMTP servers support authorization with the industry-standard OAuth 2.0 protocol.
You can add Gmail to other email clients, like Microsoft Outlook, Apple Mail, or Mozilla Thunderbird. When you add Gmail, your messages and labels are synced
